root: ^Thorgeir: Aye… stand aside. Steel cools quicker than gossip.
^ And mind the fire — last curious fool nearly left here without his eyebrows.
^What’s a typical day in your life?

c-1: ^Thorgeir: By Vael’Noor’s flame, have you seen another? Point me the way, I’d toast to the competition.
^ But no—every sword, every plough, every hinge in this town is Thorgeir’s burden.
^ With orcs sniffing at our borders, the king keeps my forge busier than a tavern on solstice night.
^Thorgeir: My father forged. His father before him.
^ Me? I spat at the trade in my youth. Raised hell, dodged the law, left my old man sick and waiting for a son who never came.
^Thorgeir: By the time I returned, it was too late. I dug his grave myself, then lifted his hammer.
^ Found that fire and rage could shape steel as well as it shaped scars. Perhaps that was his secret.
^Thorgeir: Now every blade I forge carries a piece of that penance. Some of ‘em have tasted blood—mine included.
c-2: ^Thorgeir: Hmph. Same as yesterday, same as tomorrow.
^ I rise before the cock crows, coax the forge awake while the town still dreams.
^ Then it’s bellows and sweat, hammer and sparks—nails, hinges, blades, whatever folk demand.
^Thorgeir: By midday, the heat’s like standing inside the sun. Sweat stings the eyes, burns like brine.
^ The apprentices whine their arms ache — I growl “swing or starve,” and that usually hushes ‘em.
^Thorgeir: Come evening, I quench steel in oil or water. The hiss and steam reek like blood.
^ Then I drink, to drown the hammer that never leaves my ears. Even in sleep, I hear the ringing. Always ringing.

s0: ^Thorgeir: They whisper of thieves nesting in the sewers. Waiting for what, no one dares say.
^ If my legs were younger, I’d climb down that ladder myself and find the truth.
s1: ^Thorgeir: A drunkard swore he saw a woman beckoning him out in Mountainpass.
^ Said she vanished when he drew close. I told him it was mead’s trickery—but he swore her eyes burned like coals.
